key_insight: GAIA learns geometry-aware operator mappings that work for both forward and inverse PDE problems on arbitrary domains, even when inputs and outputs live on different spatial domains.
engineering_relevance: It offers a single fast surrogate model for simulation, boundary-value, and inverse design workflows without retraining, iterative optimization, or graph construction.
method: Encodes boundary geometry and interior fields into geometry tokens.
Uses cross-attention to condition integral transform layers on local geometric features.
Supports one-pass prediction across forward, BVP, and inverse settings on arbitrary geometries.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on seven 2D/3D benchmarks, including four new or extended inverse/BVP tasks, where GAIA set new state of the art on every inverse and BVP benchmark and remained competitive on forward tasks.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on accurate geometry and tokenization; like other neural operators, robustness across extreme mesh/point-resolution shifts and unseen shape distributions may require careful validation.
paper_title: GAIA: Geometry-Adaptive Operator Learning for Forward and Inverse Problems
